sentences.original_sentence: Angela couldn't get to work because there were no trains.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Angela ................................. to work because there were no trains.
sentences.why: Prevent someone from + -ing; in the passive: was prevented from getting.

sentences.original_sentence: 'I wouldn't study biology if I were you,' said Danny.
sentences.why: Advise someone (not) to do something: the advice was not to study.

sentences.original_sentence: Prices are higher in the city than in the country.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Prices ................................. in the country as in the city.
sentences.why: Not as + adjective + as: turn a comparative round with as … as.

sentences.original_sentence: 'Jane, would you like to go for a meal after work?' said Roberto.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Roberto asked Jane ................................. for a meal after work.
sentences.why: Reported question: if/whether, and fancy + -ing (fancy going).

sentences.original_sentence: 'However hard I try, I still can't get everything done,' sighed Dr Werner.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Dr Werner complained that she couldn't get everything done, ................................. she tried.
sentences.why: No matter how + adjective/adverb: however hard = no matter how hard.

sentences.original_sentence: They will be selling tickets for the concert from Wednesday onwards.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Tickets for the concert ................................. Wednesday.
sentences.why: Passive continuous: are being sold; not … until = not before.

sentences.original_sentence: I don't know who this bag belongs to as there's no name on it.
sentences.gapped_sentence: I don't know ................................. as there's no name on it.
sentences.why: Whose + noun, and a statement order in an indirect question: whose bag this is.

sentences.original_sentence: If the economic situation doesn't improve soon, more people will lose their jobs.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Unless ................................. the economic situation soon, more people will lose their jobs.
sentences.why: There is an improvement in + noun: improve (verb) becomes improvement (noun).

sentences.original_sentence: There is no more paper left in the photocopier.
sentences.why: Run out of something: have none left.

sentences.original_sentence: 'I'd prefer you to stay at home tonight,' said Richard's father.
sentences.gapped_sentence: 'I'd ................................. go out tonight,' said Richard's father.
sentences.why: Would rather + subject + past simple: I'd rather you didn't go out.

sentences.original_sentence: There was no way David could find the right answer to the problem.
sentences.gapped_sentence: It was ................................. find the right answer to the problem.
sentences.why: It is impossible for someone to do something.

sentences.original_sentence: Kirsten isn't nearly as tidy as I am.
sentences.why: Far + comparative + than: far tidier / far more tidy than.

sentences.original_sentence: 'They've postponed tonight's football match till next Saturday,' said Jorge.
sentences.gapped_sentence: 'Tonight's football match ................................. till next Saturday,' said Jorge.
sentences.why: Put off = postpone; passive present perfect: has been put off.

sentences.original_sentence: Paula always gets angry when she makes a mistake.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Paula always ................................. when she makes a mistake.
sentences.why: Lose your temper = get angry.

sentences.original_sentence: 'I hardly slept last night,' the woman complained.
sentences.gapped_sentence: 'I had ................................. last night,' the woman complained.
sentences.why: Almost no + noun: hardly slept = had almost no sleep.

sentences.original_sentence: 'We'll talk about your proposal soon,' said the manager.
sentences.gapped_sentence: 'We'll discuss ................................. future,' said the manager.
sentences.why: In the near future = soon; discuss takes a direct object (no about).

sentences.original_sentence: Information about the new opening times was sent to all customers last week.
sentences.gapped_sentence: All customers ................................. the changes in opening times last week.
sentences.why: Inform someone about something; passive: were informed about.

sentences.original_sentence: My brother once worked as a circus clown.
sentences.gapped_sentence: My brother used ................................. as a circus clown.
sentences.why: Used to + verb for a past habit or state: used to have a job.

sentences.original_sentence: Not many people realise the amount of practice that a dancer has to do.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Very ................................. much practice a dancer has to do.
sentences.why: Very few people = not many people; understand how much.

sentences.original_sentence: Keep your passport handy because you may need to show it at customs.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Keep your passport handy in ................................. show it at customs.
sentences.why: In case + present: in case you are asked to (the possibility you prepare for).

sentences.original_sentence: Jaime was so tired he couldn't walk another step.
sentences.why: Too + adjective + to + verb: too tired to walk.

sentences.original_sentence: Peter was green with envy when he saw my new guitar.
sentences.gapped_sentence: The sight of my ................................. green with envy.
sentences.why: Make someone + adjective: the sight made Peter green with envy.

sentences.original_sentence: 'If we don't leave immediately, we'll be late,' said Linda.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Linda said they would be late if they ................................. at once.
sentences.why: Set off = leave; reported conditional: if they didn't set off.

sentences.original_sentence: Everyone thinks the company will move to Tokyo next year.
sentences.gapped_sentence: The company ................................. to Tokyo next year.
sentences.why: Be expected to + verb: the passive of expect someone to do.

sentences.original_sentence: Emma's favourite food is pasta.
sentences.why: Would rather + verb + than: would rather eat pasta than anything else.

sentences.original_sentence: How good is your relationship with your neighbours?
sentences.gapped_sentence: How well ................................. with your neighbours?
sentences.why: Get on (well) with someone = have a good relationship.

sentences.original_sentence: I showed no talent for basketball at school.
sentences.why: Be good at something; no good / not any good at = no talent for.

sentences.original_sentence: The snowstorm made it impossible for us to go skiing.
sentences.why: Prevent someone from + -ing; passive: were prevented from going.

sentences.original_sentence: We haven't heard from Anastasia since she started the job in Toronto.
sentences.gapped_sentence: We ................................. from Anastasia since she started the job in Toronto.
sentences.why: Have had no news from someone = haven't heard from them.

sentences.original_sentence: Tara can't have been telling the truth about where she got the money.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Tara ................................. about where she got the money.
sentences.why: Must have been + -ing: certainty about the past (can't have been telling the truth = must have been lying).

sentences.original_sentence: Riding a motorbike last Friday was a new experience for me.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Last Friday was the first ................................. ridden a motorbike.
sentences.why: The first time + past perfect: the first time I had ever ridden.

sentences.original_sentence: We got lost going home from the leisure centre.
sentences.gapped_sentence: We couldn't ................................. from the leisure centre.
sentences.why: Find your way home = not get lost.

sentences.original_sentence: Is it really necessary for the garage to service the car today?
sentences.gapped_sentence: Do you really need ................................. at the garage today?
sentences.why: Have something done: to have the car serviced (someone else does it).

sentences.original_sentence: This box will be too small for the present.
sentences.why: Fit in/into: the present won't fit in this box.

sentences.original_sentence: It was after midnight when Mary finished work.
sentences.why: Not … until: didn't finish work until after midnight.

sentences.original_sentence: People say that Rick is an extremely reliable person.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Rick has ................................. extremely reliable.
sentences.why: A reputation for + -ing: a reputation for being reliable.

sentences.original_sentence: The young lion didn't frighten the zoo-keeper.
sentences.gapped_sentence: The zoo-keeper ................................. the young lion.
sentences.why: Be afraid of something: wasn't afraid of the lion.

sentences.original_sentence: Nothing important happened at the meeting, so I didn't ring you.
sentences.gapped_sentence: I would have rung you ................................. at the meeting.
sentences.why: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

sentences.original_sentence: My house and the school are very close to each other.
sentences.gapped_sentence: It is only ................................. my house to the school.
sentences.why: A short distance from … to: close = a short distance.

sentences.original_sentence: My clothes aren't nearly as fashionable as yours.
sentences.why: Much + comparative + than: much more fashionable than.

sentences.original_sentence: He doesn't take any notice of what other people say about him.
sentences.gapped_sentence: He doesn't ................................. what other people say about him.
sentences.why: Pay attention to = take notice of.

sentences.original_sentence: Debbie said she would continue to work until 10 o'clock.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Debbie said she would ................................. until 10 o'clock.
sentences.why: Carry on + -ing = continue to.

sentences.original_sentence: The college will provide all the equipment students need for the course.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Students ................................. all the equipment they need for the course by the college.
sentences.why: Provide someone with something; passive: will be provided with.

sentences.original_sentence: Could you start the story again, as I'm getting confused?
sentences.gapped_sentence: Could you ................................. of the story, as I'm getting confused?
sentences.why: Go back to the start = start again.

sentences.original_sentence: We bought our train tickets in advance to avoid queuing at the station.
sentences.gapped_sentence: We bought our train tickets in advance so that ................................. queue at the station.
sentences.why: So that + would(n't): a purpose in the past; have to = need to.

sentences.original_sentence: Peter is not usually as late as this.
sentences.why: It's (not) like someone to do something: typical of them.

sentences.original_sentence: 'It isn't a good idea to go swimming after such a heavy meal,' said my aunt.
sentences.gapped_sentence: 'You ................................. swimming after such a heavy meal,' said my aunt.
sentences.why: Had better (not) + base verb: advice.

sentences.original_sentence: We have not seen Tom for over five years.
sentences.why: It is + time + since + past simple: since we last saw.

sentences.original_sentence: Diana said she was willing to help me.
sentences.why: Not mind + -ing = be willing to.

sentences.original_sentence: There's not much chance the teacher will forget to ask us for our homework.
sentences.gapped_sentence: The teacher ................................. to ask us for our homework.
sentences.why: Be unlikely to + verb: not much chance that.

sentences.original_sentence: How many cars can this company produce in a month?
sentences.why: Passive with a modal: can be produced by.

sentences.original_sentence: 'That's the last time I talk to him!' Geoff said.
sentences.why: Not going to + verb + again: the last time I talk to him.

sentences.original_sentence: While I was on holiday, a lot of interesting things happened to me.
sentences.gapped_sentence: During ................................. a lot of interesting experiences.
sentences.why: During + noun (not a clause): during my holiday I had experiences.

sentences.original_sentence: It was careless of you to leave without locking the door.
sentences.gapped_sentence: You ................................. the door before you left.
sentences.why: Ought to have + past participle: criticism of something not done.

sentences.original_sentence: 'Is Pete likely to change his mind?' Rob asked.
sentences.gapped_sentence: 'Is there ................................. changing his mind?' Rob asked.
sentences.why: Any chance of + someone + -ing.

sentences.original_sentence: Paul is the only person who has replied to the invitation.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Apart from Paul, ................................. to the invitation.
sentences.why: Apart from Paul, nobody has replied: only Paul did.

sentences.original_sentence: Are you familiar with his teaching style yet?
sentences.gapped_sentence: Have you ................................. his teaching style yet?
sentences.why: Get used to + noun or -ing = become familiar with.

sentences.original_sentence: It was such a sunny day that none of us wanted to do any work.
sentences.gapped_sentence: None of us ................................. any work because it was such a sunny day.
sentences.why: Feel like + -ing = want to.

sentences.original_sentence: Barbara couldn't sing or dance.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Besides ................................. , Barbara couldn't dance either.
sentences.why: Besides + -ing: besides being unable to sing.

sentences.original_sentence: Dinner will be served immediately upon our arrival at the hotel.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Dinner will be served ................................. at the hotel.
sentences.why: As soon as + present for the future: immediately upon arrival.

sentences.original_sentence: This piano is so heavy that we can't lift it off the ground.
sentences.gapped_sentence: This piano ................................. to lift off the ground.
sentences.why: Too + adjective + for someone + to + verb.

sentences.original_sentence: Apart from Jim, nobody objected to the plan.
sentences.why: The only one to + verb: nobody else did it.

sentences.original_sentence: Carole wanted the new mechanic to check her car.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Carole wanted ................................. by the new mechanic.
sentences.why: Have something done: to have her car checked by the mechanic.

sentences.original_sentence: Tom will have to leave for the airport soon.
sentences.gapped_sentence: It will soon ................................. for Tom to leave for the airport.
sentences.why: It is time for someone to do something.

sentences.original_sentence: We keep the keys here.
sentences.why: This is where + clause: the place where.

sentences.original_sentence: My private affairs are not your business.
sentences.why: Have nothing to do with = are not someone's business.

sentences.original_sentence: Graham took part in the race despite feeling unwell.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Graham took part in the race ................................. unwell.
sentences.why: Even though + clause = despite + -ing.

sentences.original_sentence: I've been to this museum once before.
sentences.why: My second visit = I've been once before.

sentences.original_sentence: We want someone who can do the job efficiently.
sentences.gapped_sentence: We want someone who ................................. the job efficiently.
sentences.why: Be capable of + -ing = can do.

sentences.original_sentence: Mary is bound to want to go to the football match.
sentences.gapped_sentence: There ................................. Mary will want to go to the football match.
sentences.why: There is no doubt that = is bound to.

sentences.original_sentence: Is it all right for me to use the phone?
sentences.why: Do you mind if I + present: asking permission.

sentences.original_sentence: Few people study Latin nowadays at school.
sentences.gapped_sentence: There ................................. study Latin nowadays at school.
sentences.why: There aren't many people who = few people.

sentences.original_sentence: The sports teacher asked me, 'Can you swim?'
sentences.gapped_sentence: The sports teacher wanted ................................. swim.
sentences.why: Want to know if/whether: a reported yes/no question; can becomes could.

sentences.original_sentence: I took some extra money with me in case the restaurant was expensive.
sentences.gapped_sentence: I thought the restaurant ................................. so I took some extra money with me.
sentences.why: Might be: a possibility, for in case.

sentences.original_sentence: The lorry was too wide to pass through the tunnel.
sentences.gapped_sentence: The tunnel ................................. the lorry to pass through.
sentences.why: Not + adjective + enough + for: too wide = not wide enough for.

sentences.original_sentence: He should really try to concentrate more on his studies.
sentences.why: It's time + subject + past simple: it's time he paid attention to.

sentences.original_sentence: Although the train was late, we still got to the meeting on time.
sentences.gapped_sentence: We still got to the meeting on time ................................. late.
sentences.why: Despite + noun or -ing: despite the train being late.

sentences.original_sentence: John said that he would like to discuss the matter with me again.
sentences.gapped_sentence: John expressed ................................. the matter with me again.
sentences.why: Express interest in + -ing.

sentences.original_sentence: The film was shorter than we had expected.
sentences.why: Not last as long as: shorter than = didn't last as long.

sentences.original_sentence: 'I'm sorry I damaged your car, Sheila,' said Tom.
sentences.why: Apologise for + -ing.

sentences.original_sentence: The fire in the library was discovered by a student.
sentences.gapped_sentence: It ................................. discovered the fire in the library.
sentences.why: Cleft sentence: It was a student who discovered…

sentences.original_sentence: Gerald is too young to vote.
sentences.why: Not + adjective + enough: too young = not old enough.

sentences.original_sentence: 'Do fast cars interest you?' the dealer asked Sarah.
sentences.gapped_sentence: The dealer asked Sarah ................................. in fast cars.
sentences.why: Reported question: if/whether + backshift; be interested in.

sentences.original_sentence: My brother really wishes he could sing well.
sentences.gapped_sentence: My brother regrets ................................. sing well.
sentences.why: Regret + -ing; wishes he could = regrets not being able to.

sentences.original_sentence: Maria said I had caused the accident.
sentences.why: Blame someone for something/-ing.

sentences.original_sentence: James did not need to register for the new course.
sentences.gapped_sentence: It ................................. James to register for the new course.
sentences.why: It is (not) necessary for someone to do something.

sentences.original_sentence: She never finishes her work on time although she works hard.
sentences.gapped_sentence: She never finishes her work on time ................................. she works.
sentences.why: No matter how hard: however hard she works.

sentences.original_sentence: There haven't been many changes in this town since I last visited it.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Since my last ................................. changed in this town.
sentences.why: Not much has + past participle: few changes = not much has changed.

sentences.original_sentence: Hardly anybody applied for the job.
sentences.why: Very few + noun: hardly anybody = very few applicants.

sentences.original_sentence: Luisa does a full-time job and looks after the house too.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Luisa does a full-time job ................................. the house.
sentences.why: As well as + -ing: does one thing and another too.

sentences.original_sentence: I thought the T-shirt was too expensive at £20.
sentences.why: Should have cost less than: too expensive.

sentences.original_sentence: Bad weather caused the plane to be delayed.
sentences.gapped_sentence: The plane was delayed ................................. bad weather.
sentences.why: As a result of + noun: caused by.

sentences.original_sentence: Rachel couldn't go to the cinema because she didn't have any money.
sentences.gapped_sentence: If Rachel had had some money, she ................................. to go to the cinema.
sentences.why: Third conditional: would have been able to (couldn't = not able).

sentences.original_sentence: I don't like you using my car without asking first.
sentences.gapped_sentence: I ................................. my car without asking first.
sentences.why: Wish + would(n't): annoyance at someone's behaviour.

sentences.original_sentence: Janet behaved so badly her parents wouldn't let her go to the party.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Janet's ................................. her parents wouldn't let her go to the party.
sentences.why: So + adjective + that: behaviour was so bad that.

sentences.original_sentence: Martin arranged for the agency to sell his house.
sentences.gapped_sentence: Martin arranged ................................. by the agency.
sentences.why: Have something done: to have his house sold by the agency.
